title: Dispatch LTP 8: Chronicle Press Closes Before the Crowd Arrives
summary: The editor orders the old forme removed and accepts the headline he hoped to escape.
author: Nora Finch, Harbor Gazette
paragraphs: The Chronicle did not print an edition today. At dawn, Mr. Ashcombe signed an order closing the pressroom and sent the staff home with pay. The advance issue dated today had appeared the night before. Its closure notice carried his name; its final line was now legible: “No further issue shall be struck here.”

Inspector Voss and Miss Marsh lifted the obsolete forme from beneath the floor. As they carried it across the room, its blank strips acquired the outlines of today’s unopened columns. Ashcombe ordered the type separated and the iron frame taken to the foundry. The ordinary press was shut down but left intact.

A crowd gathered anyway, having learned of the notice from copies that arrived overnight. Mr. Ashcombe went into the street and told them there would be no paper to collect and no fire to witness. Some called him a coward for surrendering the Chronicle. Others left when he held up the signed order.

There was smoke in the pressroom, though no blaze: the foundry cart’s lantern had scorched a bundle of discarded proofs. Voss extinguished it before it spread. The last advance issue’s report of a burning pressroom faded to an account of the closure and the brief alarm.

The Chronicle’s office will remain shut tomorrow. Ashcombe says the newspaper may resume from another press if no new advance issue appears. “I signed what the page said I would,” he told us. “It did not tell me why. That part was mine to decide.”
